answer: One strong defense is a bonded identity with a slow release: joining requires locking a deposit that stays frozen for a full season, and an operator cannot forge extra identities for free, because each one demands its own separate deposit. If two identities ever act in lockstep — same votes, same timing, same comet-like bursts of activity — peers investigate, and proven duplicates lose their deposits and are pruned. A violet badge on an identity therefore signals real capital at risk, not just a free account, so a Sybil army becomes as expensive as the influence it hopes to buy.
